Population decreased in Lancaster

The estimated population of Lancaster in 2024 was 145,006 usual residents.

This meant that Lancaster was among one of only eleven local authorities in England and Wales where the population did not grow.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Lancaster increased by 1.9%.

Over this slightly longer period, Lancaster was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Lancaster

The average (median) age rose to 41.1 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Lancaster has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Lancaster is an area that is classed as intermediate urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Lancaster's population of 145,006 usual residents was made up of:

  • 23,437 people aged 0 to 15 years, (16.2%)
  • 91,128 people aged 16 to 64 years, (62.8%)
  • 30,441 people aged 65 years and over, (21%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Lancaster has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (21% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Lancaster, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Lancaster
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Lancaster, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 490 people (-0.3%). In total, there were 1,166 births and 1,656 deaths in Lancaster.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 647 (-0.4%). There were 10,574 people entering the area and 11,221 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Lancaster's population of 1,108 (0.8%) as a result of 2,291 people entering the area and 1,183 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Lancaster was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Lancaster in mid-2023 is 145,056.

Within this, international migration was revised downwards by 1,243 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 740 people.

Overall, there was an revision downwards of 503 people.
